Name: Stardew i18n Translator
Author: Neko41
Description:
[center][size=6][b][color=#e3a94e]STARDEW i18n TRANSLATOR[/color][/b][/size]
[size=4]Translate SMAPI mods side by side, without digging through JSON files by hand.[/size][/center]

Why I made this: I wanted a way to translate mods without having to worry about mistyping or misreading a token somewhere. And for really big mods, say 3,000 strings, you can let AI do a first pass and then check everything yourself in Review, so AI takes some of the work off your hands.

[line]

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]What it does[/color][/b][/size]
Translating a mod usually means opening [b]i18n/default.json[/b], copying it, and hoping you didn't break a [b]$1[/b] or a [b]{{PlayerName}}[/b] somewhere in line 400. This is a small Windows app that does the tedious part for you. It scans your Mods folder, shows the English text and your translation side by side, checks every dialogue token while you type, and writes clean translation files – or one ZIP you can share.

You do the translating. AI is an extra you can switch on later if you want it.

[list]
[*][b]Pick your folders and language once.[/b] The app scans your mods and opens the workspace.[/*]
[*][b]Choose a mod[/b] and [b]double-click a string[/b] to translate it. [b]Save & next[/b] keeps you moving.[/*]
[*][b]Check the queues[/b] – Open, Changed, Review and Issues show what still needs you.[/*]
[*][b]Export…[/b] asks for this mod or all mods, and for a translation ZIP (for Mod Organizer 2, Vortex or sharing) or JSON files written straight into your mods.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Features[/color][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]All your mods in one workspace. Multi-part mods are grouped, existing translations are picked up, and every mod shows how much is done. Scanning only reads your files.[/*]
[*]Search across all mods by key, English text or translation, together with the status filters Open, Changed, Review and Done.[/*]
[*]After a mod update, the next scan tells you how many English lines were added, changed or removed, and you can open the new and changed ones. Lines you had already translated move to [b]Changed[/b], so you know what to look at again.[/*]
[*][b]Token-safe editing[/b] – dialogue codes like [b]$1[/b], [b]#$b#[/b] or [b]{{PlayerName}}[/b] are checked as you type (Content Patcher, SMAPI, mail and formatting tokens too). A missing token goes back in with one click. Harmless differences are just notes; a real error keeps only that one line out of the export, so it stays English in-game until you fix it or confirm the difference is intended.[/*]
[*][b]Issues view[/b] – every token error and warning for the current mod, or all mods, in one list, explained in plain language.[/*]
[*]Glossary hints come from your own Stardew game files (or a supported community language pack), so item, place and character names match the game. You don't need them to translate or export.[/*]
[*]Batch work: select lines with the checkboxes, Ctrl+click or Shift+click, then mark them done, keep the original, clear them, or hand them to AI or an LLM batch. The last batch edit can be undone during the session.[/*]
[*]Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Enter saves, Ctrl+Shift+Enter saves and opens the next string, and you can change them in Settings. An activity log lists the scans, saves, exports and AI runs of the session.[/*]
[*][b]Safe export[/b] – saving keeps your work in the app (separately for each language); your mods only change when you export. Export replaces the mod's translation file, the old one is kept as a [b].bak[/b] backup, and if a multi-file export fails, it's rolled back. Regional files such as [b]de-DE.json[/b], which the game would prefer over yours, are backed up and removed so players see your translation.[/*]
[*]Translation ZIPs hold one mod or all of them, with only the translation files inside. You can adjust the install folders in the preview to match the original mod.[/*]
[/list]The token checks follow the game itself: the rules were checked against Stardew Valley's own dialogue and mail code, Content Patcher and Mail Framework Mod. A line is only held back when it would really break something in the game.

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Optional AI[/color][/b][/size]
AI is optional, and none of it runs until you choose it: a local model (LM Studio or Ollama, on your PC only), your ChatGPT plan through a browser sign-in (no API key needed), or an LLM batch file you hand to any other tool. Imported batches are checked and never overwrite translations you already have. Every AI result lands in [b]Review[/b] and is never marked Done on its own. Export still includes Review text, so look it over first. Details are in the [url=https://github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator/blob/main/docs/ai.md]AI guide[/url].

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Installation[/color][/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Download the main file and [b]extract the whole ZIP[/b] to a folder you can write to (for example in Documents). There is no installer.[/*]
[*]Run [b]stardew-i18n-translator.exe[/b].[/*]
[*]Select your Stardew Valley folder, your Mods folder (the game's own, or Mod Organizer 2's mods folder) and your target language. The app scans your mods.[/*]
[*]Choose a mod, double-click a string and start translating.[/*]
[/list][b]Requirements:[/b] 64-bit Windows and the [url=https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/]Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime[/url] (already on most Windows 10/11 PCs; if it's missing, the app offers Microsoft's download page – nothing is installed automatically). The app is not signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you on the first start.

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Updating[/color][/b][/size]
The app keeps everything in a [b]data[/b] folder next to the exe: your settings, your translation work and the glossary. [b]Keep this folder when you update or move the app.[/b] Close the app, back up the whole folder, extract the new version to a new folder and copy your [b]data[/b] folder next to the new exe.

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Languages and files[/color][/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Built-in game languages:[/b] German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish and Chinese.[/*]
[*][b]Custom languages:[/b] Vietnamese, Indonesian, Ukrainian, Polish, Finnish, Dutch, Czech and Thai. To use these in the game you need a matching language mod.[/*]
[*][b]Supported files:[/b] standard SMAPI i18n files – [b]i18n/default.json[/b] and [b]i18n/<language>.json[/b], or split folders like [b]i18n/default/*.json[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Not supported:[/b] the app does not translate content.json or XNB files, does not manage mods and does not download updates.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Privacy[/color][/b][/size]
Scanning, editing, glossary, validation and export all run on your PC. No account, no analytics, no telemetry.
Local AI stays on your PC. ChatGPT sends the lines you translate and nearby context directly to OpenAI. LLM batch files leave your PC only when you upload them yourself. Details are in the [url=https://github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator/blob/main/docs/ai.md#data-and-privacy]AI guide[/url].

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Bugs and ideas[/color][/b][/size]
Please post bugs with the app version and what you did, in the bugs tab or on [url=https://github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator/issues]GitHub[/url]. [b]Settings > About[/b] opens the logs folder. Logs can contain local paths, so check them before sharing.

[size=4][b][color=#e3a94e]Source[/color][/b][/size]
Free and open source (GPL-3.0-or-later): [url=https://github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator]github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator[/url]. Downloads, the [url=https://github.com/Nana1873/stardew-i18n-translator/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md]user guide[/url] and the changelog are there too.

Built with substantial help from AI coding agents. I use the app for my own German translations, decide what gets built and what ships, and spot-check each release on real mods on top of the automated tests.
The AI tag on this page refers to how the code was written. The app itself works fully without AI.
